title: The Behavioral Rate of Fine-Tuning: Compression as a Measure of Useful Information
abstract: arXiv:2611.06598v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) adapts a frozen language model through a compact learned update, making it a natural setting for asking how much information fine-tuning needs to write. Yet adapter rank, parameter count, or numerical reconstruction error do not directly tell us how many bits are required to preserve the acquired behavior. We therefore define an operational behavioral rate $R^\star$ as the smallest serialized size of a compressed adapter that, once reloaded into the frozen base model, retains a fixed fraction of its held-out fine-tuning gain. Across LoRA fine-tuning experiments, this rate increases with distinct training content at fixed optimization budgets, but is not determined by intuitive metrics like source description length, fine-tuning gain, or weight-space reconstruction error. translated_title: 微调的行为速率：将压缩作为有用信息的度量
translated_abstract: 低秩适应通过对冻结的语言模型施加一个紧凑的学习更新来对其进行适配，这为探究“微调需要写入多少信息”提供了一个自然的研究场景。然而，适配器的秩、参数量或数值重建误差并不能直接告诉我们需要多少比特才能保留所获得的行为。因此，我们定义了一个可操作的行为速率 $R^\star$：即压缩后的适配器在重新加载回冻结基础模型后，仍能保留其留出集微调增益的固定比例时所需的最小序列化大小。在LoRA微调实验中，该速率在固定优化预算下随训练内容的不同而增加，但并不由源描述长度、微调增益或权重空间重建误差等直观指标所决定。最重要的是，相同的数据集在不同的冻结基础模型上表现出显著不同、甚至重新排序的速率，这表明微调所写入的信息依赖于其作用的基础模型。
tldr: 本文提出“行为速率 $R^\star$”这一新指标——以能保留固定比例微调增益的压缩适配器最小序列化大小来度量微调写入的有用信息，并发现该速率由训练内容与冻结基础模型共同决定，而非参数量、微调增益或重建误差等直观指标。
en_tdlr: This paper defines an operational "behavioral rate" $R^\star$ — the smallest compressed adapter size that preserves a fixed fraction of fine-tuning gain — showing that the useful information written by fine-tuning depends on both training content and the frozen base model, rather than on intuitive metrics like rank, gain, or reconstruction error.
